analysis.investment_thesis: HEG is a textbook commodity-cycle business — graphite electrode prices boom with steel EAF demand and collapse just as violently, making durable wealth creation near-impossible. At 32x P/E on deeply depressed earnings (ROE 2.59%, net profit collapsed from ₹3,026 Cr in FY19 to ₹115 Cr in FY25), the market is pricing in a recovery that may or may not arrive.
key_strengths: Conservative balance sheet — D/E of just 0.14 with ₹4,627 Cr reserves is genuinely sound
Promoter holding stable at 56.27% with no visible reduction — integrity signal
Gross margin of 58.7% suggests real pricing power at the top of the cycle
key_risks: Catastrophic earnings volatility — net profit swung ₹3,026 Cr (FY19) → -₹18 Cr (FY21) → ₹115 Cr (FY25); entirely at the mercy of global steel EAF cycles
ROE of 2.59% and ROCE of 3.96% are far below my 15% minimum — capital is being destroyed in real terms
32x P/E on trough earnings is dangerous; if the next down-cycle arrives before recovery, stock could halve
red_flags: Earnings variance of 100x between peak (FY19) and trough (FY21) — no business with this volatility belongs in a long-term portfolio
FCF deeply negative two consecutive years (FY22: -₹499 Cr, FY23: -₹364 Cr) while capex was high — capital allocation risk
Other income (₹145 Cr in FY25) is nearly equal to operating profit (₹255 Cr) — core business barely earning anything at current cycle
analysis.detailed_analysis:
HEG is a pure commodity cyclical — graphite electrode demand is a derivative of Electric Arc Furnace steel production, which is itself cyclical. The revenue history tells the entire story: ₹859 Cr (FY17) → ₹6,591 Cr (FY19, supercycle peak driven by China supply curbs) → ₹1,254 Cr (FY21) → ₹2,158 Cr (FY25). This is not a business — this is a lottery ticket tied to Chinese steel policy and global scrap availability. No amount of management quality can overcome a business model that produces ₹3,026 Cr net profit one year and loses money the next. I built DMart on predictable demand — people eat every day. Nobody needs graphite electrodes at a steady rate.

The balance sheet is the one redeeming feature: D/E of 0.14 means the company will survive the downturn, as it did in FY20-21. But surviving is not compounding. With ROE at 2.59% today and ₹4,666 Cr of equity deployed, shareholders are earning ₹121 Cr — barely above inflation. The market cap of ₹12,215 Cr values this at 32x those trough earnings. Forward P/E of 22x assumes a meaningful recovery, but graphite electrode prices are determined by forces entirely outside management's control. This is speculation, not investing.
